judges.18.p1.b1.text: In those days there was no king in Israel, and the tribe of the Danites was looking for territory to occupy.

judges.18.p1.b2.text: So the Danites sent out five men from their clans, men of valor from Zorah and Eshtaol, to spy out the land and explore it.

judges.18.p1.b4.text: The men entered the hill country of Ephraim and came to the house of Micah, where they spent the night.

judges.18.p2.b1.text: Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place? Why are you here?

judges.18.p2.b2.text: Micah has done this and that for me, … and he has hired me to be his priest.

judges.18.p2.b3.text: Please inquire of God to determine whether we will have a successful journey.

judges.18.p2.b4.text: Go in peace. The LORD is watching over your journey.

judges.18.p3.b1.text: So the five men departed and came to Laish, where they saw that the people were living securely, … and had no alliance with anyone.

judges.18.p3.b3.text: Come on, let us go up against them, … for God has delivered it into your hand. It is a place where nothing on earth is lacking.

judges.18.p4.b1.text: So six hundred Danites departed from Zorah and Eshtaol, armed with weapons of war.

judges.18.p4.b2.text: They went up and camped at Kiriath-jearim in Judah. That is why the place west of Kiriath-jearim is called Mahaneh-dan to this day.

judges.18.p4.b3.text: Did you know that one of these houses has an ephod, household gods, a graven image, and a molten idol? Now think about what you should do.

judges.18.p5.b1.text: So they turned aside there and went to the home of the young Levite, the house of Micah, and greeted him. The six hundred Danites stood at the entrance of the gate, armed with their weapons of war.

judges.18.p5.b3.text: Be quiet, … Put your hand over your mouth and come with us … Is it better for you to be a priest for the house of one person or a priest for a tribe and family in Israel?

judges.18.p5.b4.text: So the priest was glad and took the ephod, the household idols, and the graven image, and went with the people.

judges.18.p6.b1.text: Putting their small children, their livestock, and their possessions in front of them, they turned and departed.

judges.18.p6.b2.text: What is the matter with you that you have called out such a company?

judges.18.p6.b3.text: You took the gods I had made, and my priest, and went away. What else do I have?

judges.18.p6.b4.text: Do not raise your voice against us, or angry men will attack you, …

judges.18.p6.b5.text: and Micah turned to go back home, because he saw that they were too strong for him.

judges.18.p7.b1.text: After they had taken Micah’s idols and his priest, they went to Laish, to a tranquil and unsuspecting people, and they struck them with their swords and burned down the city.

judges.18.p7.b2.text: There was no one to deliver them, because the city was far from Sidon and had no alliance with anyone; … And the Danites rebuilt the city and lived there.

judges.18.p7.b3.text: They named it Dan, after their forefather Dan, who was born to Israel—though the city was formerly named Laish.

judges.18.p8.b1.text: The Danites set up idols for themselves,

judges.18.p8.b2.text: and Jonathan son of Gershom, the son of Moses, and his sons were priests for the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity of the land.

judges.18.p8.b3.text: So they set up for themselves Micah’s graven image, and it was there the whole time the house of God was in Shiloh.
